tytul: Red currant juice from a steam juicer (UC Master Food Preservers)
wstep: This card applies the UC Master Food Preservers method for canning high-acid fruit juice made in a steam juicer, in a boiling-water bath, to red currants only. [T:SLO-108,SLO-203,SLO-324]

akapity: UC lists the high-acid juices that may be canned with this recipe, among them berries (except elderberries) and currants. [T:SLO-052]
Currants are on this list (the guide spells them “currents”). [T:SLO-052]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): use this card only for red currants; UC lists currants without naming a colour, and no source we have read says that this method covers blackcurrants. [T:SLO-324]

Do not use it for low-acid or borderline juices, alone or mixed with the listed ones; UC excludes, among others, Asian pears, bananas, coconut, dates, elderberries, figs, ripe mangoes, melons, papaya, white peaches and nectarines, persimmons, prickly pear and tomatoes, and says the list is not complete. [T:SLO-052]

sekcje.naglowek: Why the juice must be processed
akapity: UC warns that pouring steam-juicer juice straight into sterilized jars, capping them and storing them at room temperature without further processing (“bottling”) is not safe. [T:SLO-051]
NCHFP: jars of fruit juice must be processed in a boiling-water canner long enough to destroy spoilage organisms. [T:SLO-050]
According to UC, if you do not can the juice, keep it in the refrigerator for up to one week; for longer storage, freeze it. [T:SLO-207]
According to UC, freeze juice in freezer-safe containers, such as metal or rigid plastic containers or glass jars, and leave headspace because juice expands when frozen. [T:SLO-214]

For juice, NCHFP gives 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace for a pint (about 0.47 l) and 1 inch (about 2.5 cm) for a quart (about 0.95 l) in wide-mouth containers, and 1 1/2 inches (about 3.8 cm) for both sizes in narrow-top containers. [T:SLO-222]
UC recommends straight-sided glass jars for freezing, to help prevent breakage. [T:SLO-214]
According to UC, use good-quality fruit that is ripe but not overripe, and throw out any damaged or moldy fruit. [T:SLO-211]
UC recommends not using windfall fruit, which has fallen to the ground, for juice or for canning. [T:SLO-211]
Extract the juice according to your steam juicer’s instructions; if necessary, strain it through a sieve or cheesecloth to remove seeds. [T:SLO-202]
In a clean, non-reactive saucepan, heat the juice just to a boil, with sugar to taste if you like, stirring until the sugar dissolves. [T:SLO-202]
According to UC, ladle the hot juice into hot jars, leaving 1/4 inch (about 0.6 cm) of headspace. [T:SLO-202]
Wipe the rims with a damp, clean paper towel or cloth, put on the lids and screw the bands on only fingertip-tight. [T:SLO-202]
According to UC, at 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m) process pint and quart jars for 15 minutes. [T:SLO-203,ACI-176]
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased. [T:ACI-015]
According to UC, at 1001–3000 ft (above 300 m up to 900 m) process them for 20 minutes. [T:SLO-203,ACI-176]
According to UC, at 3001–6000 ft (above 900 m up to 1800 m) process them for 25 minutes. [T:SLO-203,ACI-176]
According to UC, at 6001–8000 ft (above 1800 m up to 2400 m) process them for 30 minutes. [T:SLO-203,ACI-176,SLO-209]
Above 8000 ft (above 2400 m) UC gives no time, so this card does not cover canning at that elevation. [T:SLO-203,SLO-209]
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m, 3000 ft becomes 900 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m. [T:ACI-176]
8000 ft (2438.4 m) becomes 2400 m, so the range without a time is wider than in the source. [T:SLO-209]
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage. [T:ACI-015]
These times are for US jar sizes: a pint holds about 473 ml and a quart about 946 ml. [T:ACI-174]
JarAtlas rule (the source does not test metric jars): for a jar of up to 473 ml use the pint time, and for a larger jar of up to 946 ml, for example 0.5 l or 0.9 l, use the quart time. [T:SLO-208]
UC gives no time for these juices in jars larger than a quart, such as liter jars, so JarAtlas recommends smaller jars. [T:SLO-203,SLO-208]
According to UC, after processing, turn off the heat, remove the canner lid and wait 5 minutes before taking the jars out. [T:SLO-204]
When you take the hot jars out of the canner, do not retighten the lids or bands; this can cut through the gasket and cause seal failures. [T:SLO-210]

Cool the jars at room temperature for 12 to 24 hours, then remove only the screw bands (the metal rings of two-piece lids), leaving the flat lids on the jars, and test the seal: press the middle of the lid, and if it springs up when you release it, the jar is not sealed. [T:SLO-196,SLO-212]

NCHFP calls Mason-type canning jars with self-sealing two-piece lids (a flat lid and a screw band) the best choice, and this seal test and the method on this card assume them; NCHFP does not recommend other commercial jars whose mouths cannot be sealed with two-piece canning lids for canning any food at home. [T:SLO-223,SLO-212]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): use this card only with jars that take two-piece canning lids; it gives no method for twist-off jars or jars with glass lids, so do not use them for this recipe. [T:SLO-223]
A sealed lid is concave, curved down slightly in the centre; if the centre is flat or bulging, the jar may not be sealed. [T:SLO-196]
If a jar has not sealed at this check, keep it in the refrigerator and eat it within several days. [T:SLO-197]

Store sealed jars in a clean, cool, dark, dry place, not above 95 °F (35 °C) and not near hot pipes, a stove or a furnace, in an uninsulated attic or in direct sunlight; in such conditions the food may spoil. [T:SLO-198]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): keep an opened jar in the refrigerator and use it within 1 week. [T:SLO-322]
Before using a stored jar, check that the lid is tight and holds a vacuum: a good seal has a concave centre. [T:SLO-191]
Look for streaks of dried food running from the top of the jar, rising air bubbles and unnatural colour. [T:SLO-191]
When opening the jar, check for an unnatural smell, spurting liquid and cotton-like mould on the food or under the lid. [T:SLO-191]
Do not taste food from a jar with an unsealed lid or with signs of spoilage. [T:SLO-190]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): throw out such a jar. [T:SLO-190]
